info.description:
Universal Notification Hub API provides endpoints for managing notification channels, distribution lists, notification templates, and dispatch. All endpoints are served under the /v1 prefix.

AUTHORIZATION. A valid bearer token authorizes nothing on its own. Every /v1 endpoint is gated on a UNH capability, and the capability is determined BY PATH PREFIX:

* `/v1/admin/*` — the **administration** capability. Granted to any tenant role listed in the service's `authz.admin_roles` (env `AUTHZ_ADMIN_ROLES`); recommended name `unh_admin`.
* `/v1/notification/*` — the **send** capability. Granted to any tenant role listed in `authz.sender_roles` (env `AUTHZ_SENDER_ROLES`, recommended `unh_sender`), and also conferred by the administration capability so an administrator can test-send.

Both lists FAIL CLOSED: an empty or absent list denies that capability outright, so a service deployed without `authz` configuration answers 403 to everything. Liveness/readiness probes and this documentation are the only unauthenticated surfaces.

A 403 response names the missing capability and the configuration key that grants it, so the message is actionable without consulting these docs. It does not echo the configured role names.

post.description:
Binds data into the template, resolves its distribution list (via UNH's own IAMS service identity — the caller needs no IAMS privilege), and dispatches to each enabled channel. Per-channel fire-and-report; one channel failing does not fail the request. A failure to read IAMS at all does fail it: 500 when IAMS rejects UNH's credentials, 503 when IAMS is unreachable.
Requires the **send** capability — a tenant role listed in `authz.sender_roles`, which gates the whole `/v1/notification/` prefix. The administration capability also confers it.

auth_method.description: none|plain. 'plain' requires an encrypted connection and credentials.

ca_cert.description:
Optional PEM trust material for this channel's relay. Public, so unlike
Password it is returned on read. Rejected when encryption is none.

encryption.description:
none|starttls|tls. 'starttls' REQUIRES the upgrade; 'none' is for a local
relay that originates TLS upstream. The port never influences it.

password.description:
Password is required when auth_method is plain, and MUST be empty when it
is none. Write-only: never returned on read.

sender_name.description: SenderName is the optional From-header display name (e.g. "Ops Team").

username.description:
Username is required when auth_method is plain, and MUST be empty when it
is none. Note auth_method defaults to plain, so omitting both this and
auth_method is rejected rather than treated as an unauthenticated relay.

editor_json.description:
EditorJSON is the visual-editor source for the body —
an arbitrary JSON object, stored verbatim and read back to re-hydrate
the editor. Optional; the rendered HTML in `body` is what gets sent.

ca_cert.description: Public trust material, so unlike password it IS returned on read (D8).

BearerAuth.description: Type "Bearer" followed by a space and JWT token.
